name: Anti-NMDA Receptor Encephalitis Psychiatric Presentation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Graus et al. 2016 Diagnostic Criteria for Autoimmune Encephalitis

criteria.description: Prominent psychiatric symptoms including psychosis, agitation, or catatonia
Detection of anti-NMDA receptor antibodies in cerebrospinal fluid or serum
Presence of neurological signs such as seizures, movement disorders, or autonomic instability
CSF pleocytosis or oligoclonal bands supportive of inflammation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of psychiatric symptoms plus detection of anti-NMDA receptor antibodies in CSF or serum
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Neurological symptoms often follow psychiatric presentation; antibody testing in CSF is more sensitive than serum.

common.symptomName: Dyskinesias including orofacial and limb movements
Autonomic instability (e.g., tachycardia, blood pressure fluctuations)

laboratory: Positive anti-NMDA receptor antibodies in CSF and/or serum
imaging: Brain MRI often normal or shows transient T2/FLAIR hyperintensities in medial temporal lobes or cerebral cortex
other: EEG showing diffuse slowing or extreme delta brush pattern
Detection of underlying ovarian teratoma or other neoplasm in some cases

distinguishingFeatures: Chronic course without rapid neurological deterioration
Distinct clinical features such as faciobrachial dystonic seizures

redFlags: Rapid progression of psychiatric symptoms with neurological deterioration
New onset seizures or movement disorders in psychiatric patient
references: Graus F, Titulaer MJ, Balu R, et al. A clinical approach to diagnosis of autoimmune encephalitis. Lancet Neurol. 2016 Apr;15(4):391-404.
Dalmau J, Lancaster E, Martinez-Hernandez E, et al. Clinical experience and laboratory investigations in patients with anti-NMDAR encephalitis. Lancet Neurol. 2011 Jan;10(1):63-74.

Titulaer MJ, McCracken L, Gabilondo I, et al. Treatment and prognostic factors for long-term outcome in patients with anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis: an observational cohort study. Lancet Neurol. 2013 Feb;12(2):157-65.
